Pluto has its own small i18n engine. It has no `@nuxtjs/i18n` dependency. It translates the admin UI. With a separate scope, it also translates the public site.

The shipped languages are `en` (the default) and `pt-BR`. A new language is a new set of JSON files. It needs no code change.

The message format is compatible with vue-i18n. Use `{name}` for values and ` | ` for plural forms.

## Locale files

Each layer, and the app, keeps its text in `i18n/locales/<code>.json`. The files of all layers merge by locale, with the base layer first and the app last. The app overrides the text of a layer.

Each layer owns one top-level namespace. It is the `$meta.name` of the layer.

| Namespace | Owner |
| --- | --- |
| `pluto` | Core. Shared words go in `pluto.common.*`. |
| `supabase`, `supabase-storage`, `supabase-shop`, `supabase-blog` | The matching layer |
| `nuxtContent` | The `@plutocms/nuxt-content` layer |
| `content.<typeName>.*` | The layer that declares the content type |
| `site.*` | The text of your public site |

## Options

Set the options under `plutoI18n` in `nuxt.config.ts`. All are optional.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `defaultLocale` | `en` | The fallback, and the last choice of every resolve order. |
| `adminLocales` | Every discovered locale | The languages that the admin offers. |
| `siteLocales` | Every discovered locale | The languages that the public site can use. |
| `siteLocale` | `defaultLocale` | The site language before a visitor picks one. |

Restart the dev server after you add a new language, so the option defaults pick it up.

## Two scopes

The admin and the site each have an active locale.

- `usePlutoI18n()` is the admin scope. It is per user.
- `usePlutoSiteI18n()` is the site scope. Your app owns it. It does not follow the admin language.

Both return `{ locale, locales, uiLocale, t, tx, te, n, d, setLocale }`.

| Function | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `t(key, params?)` | Translates a key. A number as the second argument is the plural count. |
| `tx(value)` | Translates a key or a literal. It translates only when the value looks like a key and the key exists. |
| `te(key)` | Tells if a key exists. |
| `n(value, options?)` | Formats a number with `Intl`. |
| `d(value, options?)` | Formats a date with `Intl`. |

If a key is missing, `t` falls back to the active locale, then `en`, then the key itself. In development, a missing key warns once.

### Plurals

A message with ` | ` has plural forms. Three forms are `zero | one | other`. Two forms are `one | other`. Use `t(key, count)`. It also sets `{count}`.

## Choose the first locale

- **Admin.** The cookie `pluto-admin-locale`, then the browser language matched to `adminLocales`, then `defaultLocale`.
- **Site.** The cookie `pluto-site-locale`, then the `siteLocale` option, then `defaultLocale`.

The server reads `Accept-Language`. The client reads `navigator.languages`.

## The admin language of a user

The Settings page has a "Your preferences" card with a language select. The first choice is **Automatic (browser)**. Each language shows in its own name.

A change switches the admin at once. The cookie `pluto-admin-locale` keeps the choice. If a backend layer registers a `localeDriver`, the choice is also saved there. Without a driver, the choice lives in the cookie only.

```ts
localeDriver: {
  load: async () => 'pt-BR', // or null for Automatic
  save: async (locale) => { /* store it */ }
}
```

## Translate a component

1. Call `const { t, n, d } = usePlutoI18n()` in `<script setup>`.
2. Replace each literal with `t('pluto.<area>.<name>')`.
3. Pass a value as a parameter. Never build a sentence from pieces in code. The word order differs between languages.
4. Add the key to every locale file. The files need the same keys, the same placeholders, and the same number of plural forms.
5. Format numbers and dates with `n()` and `d()`.
6. Use a getter for `useHead`, so a language switch updates the title: `useHead({ title: () => t('pluto.pages.settings') })`.
7. Read `t()` inside a template or a `computed`.

## Content type text

A content type keeps English literals. Core looks for these keys and falls back to the literal:

- `content.<name>.label`, `content.<name>.labelPlural`, `content.<name>.new`
- `content.<name>.fields.<field>.label`, `.description`, `.placeholder`
- `content.<name>.fields.<field>.options.<value>`
- `content.<name>.status.<value>`

`usePlutoContentText(type)` resolves them. The layer that declares the type owns the keys.

## Registry text

A registry entry holds a key or a literal. The consumer composables resolve it with `tx()`. A language switch updates the text.

## Validation messages

`validateContentPayload` returns errors with a `message` in English, a `code`, and `params`. The codes are `required`, `number`, `integer`, `min`, `max`, `boolean`, `option`, and `maxLength`. Each code has a key `pluto.validation.<code>`.

## Server errors

A server route throws `createPlutoError({ statusCode, message, key, params?, data? })`. The `statusMessage` stays English. The response also holds `data.i18n = { key, params }`.

On the client, `usePlutoErrorText()` returns `(error, fallbackKey?) => string`. It uses the translated `data.i18n`, then the response message, then the translated fallback key. The default fallback is `pluto.errors.unknown`.

## Nuxt UI and the `html` tag

Nuxt UI has one locale for each page. `PlutoRoot` passes the admin locale to `UApp` on routes under `/admin`, and the site locale on the other routes.

`PlutoRoot` sets `<html lang dir>` from the admin locale on routes under `/admin`. On the other routes, it sets them from the site locale only when your app uses the site scope. That means the app sets `plutoI18n.siteLocale` or `plutoI18n.siteLocales`. Otherwise, the app keeps its own `app.head.htmlAttrs`.

## Not translated

- Text stored in the database, such as categories, availability names, and roles.
- The 404 of the generated content pages.
- Server logs.
